text:
ava: hey team, hitting a weird issue on my first day  my app container can't resolve the postgres service by name when I run docker-compose up on mac (m1).
ava: I have ENV DB_HOST=postgres in the app, but I get `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND postgres` inside the app.
ava: docker-compose version: 1.29.2, Docker Desktop 4.x on mac m1.
ava: here's the minimal compose I'm using:
ava: ```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  app:
    build: .
    environment:
      - DB_HOST=postgres
    depends_on:
      - postgres
    networks:
      - backend
  postgres:
    image: postgres:13-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: example
    networks:
      - backend
networks:
  backend:
    driver: bridge
```
ava: if I `docker-compose exec app ping postgres` it hangs, but `docker ps` shows both containers.
ava: I tried `network_mode: host` as a test and it made things worse.
ava: any obvious newbie mistake? :grimacing:
sam: welcome! big +1 for the compose snippet. couple quick checks: are both services in same project/network? the `bridge` driver is fine.
sam: can you paste output of `docker network ls` and `docker network inspect <your_project>_backend`?
ava: here's `docker network ls` (filtered):
ava: ```
NETWORK ID     NAME                      DRIVER   SCOPE
abc123         myrepo_backend             bridge   local
```
ava: `docker network inspect myrepo_backend` shows both container IDs under "Containers".
maria: are you running `docker-compose up` from the same folder where compose file is named `docker-compose.yml`? if the project name changes, service DNS changes to `<project>_servicename` sometimes.
ava: file is named `docker-compose.yml` and I `docker-compose up --build`. project name is default (folder name `myrepo`).
ava: I tried `getent hosts postgres` inside the app container and it returns nothing.
jon: two quick possibilities: 1) app container's resolv.conf is weird on mac+docker desktop; 2) you're running the app binary with custom DNS resolution (node might be using c-ares). what language/runtime?
ava: node 18, using pg client.
jon: node+pg can be sensitive. try forcing DNS to be via libc by setting environment `NODE_OPTIONS=--dns-result-order=ipv4first` (or the other way around) or run `dig postgres` if `dig` is available.
ava: `dig` not installed in image. I added `apt-get update && apt-get install -y dnsutils` and then `dig postgres` -> `;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached`.
ava: weirdly, `curl http://postgres:5432` returns an empty response but exit code 0 (so name resolves to an IP?).
sam: can you `docker-compose exec app cat /etc/hosts` and `cat /etc/resolv.conf`?
ava: `/etc/hosts` has typical entries for localhost only. `/etc/resolv.conf` points to `nameserver 127.0.0.11`.
ava: `ping 172.20.0.2` (the IP I found from `docker inspect postgres`) works from app. so name resolution is the problem.
kevin: heads up  Docker's embedded DNS should populate container /etc/hosts for service names. but node's DNS lookup sometimes bypasses it due to IPv6/IPv4 ordering. also if your app sets `DNS` or `--network host` it'll break.
kevin: try setting `extra_hosts` in compose as a temporary workaround: `extra_hosts: - \"postgres:172.20.0.2\"`  not ideal but diagnostic.
ava: added extra_hosts and now app connects. so definitely DNS path.
ava: is there a recommended base image or minimal Dockerfile tweak for node apps to avoid this on mac?
junior-bot: Hi Ava! Please check the devex docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/run/local-dev#compose-dns and ping `@devex` if still stuck.
maria: Long term: prefer using the service name (postgres) + internal network. For node, try `alpine` vs `buster` images  musl vs glibc differences can affect c-ares. also ensure `libc` name resolution is used: adding `npm install --save pg-native` won't help, but `NODE_OPTIONS=--dns-result-order=ipv4first` or setting `PGHOST=postgres` can workaround.
sam: also make sure you don't have stale `/etc/hosts` overrides from dev tools (some dev kits inject entries).
ava: thanks  added `NODE_OPTIONS=--dns-result-order=ipv4first` and removed `network_mode: host`. working now locally.
ava: any tips for making sure my Dockerfile has dnsutils for future debugging?
maria: don't bake dnsutils into production image. add a separate debug image or a Makefile target like `make dev-shell` that runs `docker run --network myrepo_backend --rm -it imagename sh` and you can `apk add --no-cache bind-tools` when needed.
sam: ok closing loop  if you want I'll add a short snippet to the onboarding README on how to debug compose DNS on mac. small PR?
ava: yes please, that would have saved me an hour. :pray:
kevin: noted  also file a tiny ticket for the devex doc to mention node DNS weirdness on mac M1.
ava: thanks everyone! feeling less lost.
ava: tagging `@maria` for a quick 15m pairing if you have time to help me add the README snippet.
maria: happy to pair, afternoon works for me.
ava: awesome  will DM schedule.
